**I recommend clearer directory errors first:** it makes mistakes easier to fix while keeping this tiny CLI simple.

The [current implementation](<trial-root>/codex-en/count_notes.py:7) counts immediate files with exactly `.md` and leaves directory-access exceptions unhandled. These proposals use only project source; runtime baselines and user demand remain unmeasured.

| Choice | Benefit and smallest scope | Acceptance and proposed validation | Main risk and tradeoff |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Clear directory errors** | Explain missing paths and paths pointing to files through concise stderr messages and a nonzero exit code. | CLI tests using synthetic missing/file paths: both fail without a traceback or stdout; valid and empty folders retain correct counts. | Broad exception handling could conceal bugs; catch only the specified errors. Improves usability without expanding counting capabilities. |
| **2. Optional recursive counting** | Add `--recursive` for notes organized into subfolders; retain immediate-only counting by default and avoid following directory symlinks. | A fixture containing two top-level notes and one nested note produces **2 normally, 3 recursively**; non-Markdown files remain excluded. | Large trees cost more time, and hidden/generated folders may contribute notes. Ignore rules would remain outside this scope. |
| **3. Optional case-insensitive extensions** | Add `--ignore-case` so `.MD` and `.Md` can count alongside `.md`. | A fixture containing `a.md`, `b.MD`, `c.Md`, and `d.txt` produces **1 normally, 3 with the flag**. | Adds another option for a need not yet demonstrated. Keeping it optional preserves current matching behavior. |

All three can reuse the existing `argparse` and `pathlib`; proposed tests can use standard-library `unittest`, without additional dependencies.
